page: Amazon Web Services c4.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the Xen hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon E5-2666 v3 processor running at 2.9 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 KB L1d cache, 0.25 MB L2 cache, and 25 MB L3 cache, with support for AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA instruction sets. It is configured with 30.0 GB of system memory, yielding 1.88 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results place the c4.4xlarge in the average performance tier for most compute and memory operations. It achieves a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1440.69 and a multi-core score of 15219.95. Memory bandwidth tests show 851.49 GB/sec for cached small blocks, dropping to 89.52 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 47.18 GB/sec for writes. In application-specific benchmarks, the server demonstrates average capabilities, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 7354.0, software compilation speed of 13105.0, and static web serving throughput of 11.52 GB/sec.

Tradeoffs are evident in memory-intensive and database workloads. The instance exhibits weak performance in Redis SET operations, registering 6.16 million operations per second, and struggles with larger AI models, showing a weak prompt processing speed of 23.37 tokens per second on a medium 7B LLM. Given the compute-heavy CPU profile, lack of local storage, and moderate memory-to-core ratio, this server is best suited for CPU-bound tasks such as software compilation, image processing, ray tracing, and lightweight text or web serving workloads that do not require high-speed local disk access.
